provenance.gatheredBy: load-sport-data, the 2026 US Open men's and women's singles as played: each 128-player draw, its 32 seeds and every match's winner and sets from Wikipedia's draw pages, cross-checked match by match against ESPN's US Open scoreboard, which agrees on every pairing, winner and set count (254 matches). Match times (scheduledAt) are ESPN's. A match's score is sets won; the two men's retirements (Moutet to Sweeny in the first round, Blockx to Khachanov in the quarterfinals) count only the sets finished. Each draw's 16 qualifier places are play-in places whose playInWinner is the qualifier who filled it, named on both the draw and the qualifying pages. The lucky losers who replaced withdrawals (Ruud, the 19th men's seed, among them) are in the field as they played, unseeded, so the men's draw has 31 seeds. Each quarter of the draw is a region through the quarterfinals. Seeds' rankings are Wikipedia's (as of August 31, 2026). The unseeded players' rankings are not on the fetched pages: they rank after the seeds in the order of ESPN's ATP and WTA rankings of October 21, 2026, then in draw order, so they are an ordering, not the real ranking; qualifier places and qualifiers rank last. A player's country is Wikipedia's flag; a neutral athlete, who has none there, takes ESPN's (from its scoreboard notes, else its rankings' citizenship). Odds to win are made up, in seed order and then ranking order.
